boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along practical Seaside and Marina corridors around CSUMB, each paired with one directly sourced reason to stop.

cards.title: Read the Dunes and Fort Ord Landscape
cards.subtitle: At the west end of the 9th Street corridor
cards.notes: Follow 9th Street to the designated park entrance, then use the educational panels to interpret the dunes and former Army landscape.
cards.short_summary: A coastal trailhead where natural habitat and Fort Ord history share the view.
cards.evidence_claim: California State Parks says the park has four miles of beach, hiking and bike trails, and eight educational panels about Fort Ord and natural history.
cards.access_notes: Open 8 a.m. to sunset. Use designated roads and trails; current construction detours and trail closures may apply.

cards.title: Take a Kite to the Coast
cards.subtitle: At the western end of Reservation Road
cards.notes: Continue west on Reservation Road to the beach, bring layers, and keep water activities off the plan because the posted rip-current warning is serious.
cards.short_summary: Reservation Road ends at a dune-backed beach suited to kites, picnics, and coastal views.
cards.evidence_claim: California State Parks places the beach at the end of Reservation Road and identifies kite flying, picnic areas, interpretive exhibits, and panoramic bay views.
cards.access_notes: Open 8 a.m. to sunset. Dogs are prohibited, and California State Parks warns that water recreation is extremely hazardous due to strong rip currents.

cards.title: Pause Beside Marina’s Wetland
cards.subtitle: Along the West Reservation Road corridor
cards.notes: Turn off Reservation Road for a daylight wetland pause, respect restoration work, and observe the pond without entering vegetated habitat.
cards.short_summary: A named community wetland interrupts Marina’s western gateway with pond habitat.
cards.evidence_claim: Marina’s official records identify Locke-Paddon as a wetland community park and describe active pond, vegetation, maintenance, and public-access planning.
cards.source_title: Resolution No. 2024-109: Management of the Locke-Paddon Wetland Community Park
cards.access_notes: Visit only established public areas and heed any restoration or access notices; the source describes ongoing vegetation and access planning.

cards.entity_name: Glorya Jean Tate Park & Pump Track
cards.title: Roll the Pump Track
cards.subtitle: Beside the Reservation Road corridor
cards.notes: Enter from Reservation Road with a bike or scooter, check posted conditions, and pair the pump track with the park’s courts or exercise area.
cards.short_summary: A wheeled-sports stop backed by courts, fitness space, and a playground.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Marina documents a professionally designed pump track plus basketball, pickleball, exercise, playground, dog-park, gazebo, and cornhole amenities.
cards.source_title: Glorya Jean Tate Park & Pump Track
cards.access_notes: City park rules prohibit presence from one hour after sunset until sunrise without prior authorization; the city may close facilities for maintenance.

cards.title: Settle Into a Study Room
cards.subtitle: On Seaside Circle near Reservation Road
cards.notes: Turn from Reservation Road onto Seaside Circle, ask about a study room, and use the public computers or free Wi-Fi for a focused work session.
cards.short_summary: A county library stop with study rooms, technology, and student support.
cards.evidence_claim: Monterey County lists two study rooms, public computers, free wireless internet, and a Tuesday-through-Thursday Student Support Center at this branch.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday 11 a.m.–7 p.m., Wednesday 11 a.m.–7 p.m., Thursday 10 a.m.–6 p.m., and Friday–Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m.

cards.title: Bring the Bike to the Shop
cards.subtitle: On the General Stilwell Drive retail corridor
cards.notes: Use General Stilwell Drive to reach the store, then bring a clean bike for service evaluation or browse equipment for nearby trails.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor retailer whose on-site bike shop makes the stop more than a gear run.
cards.evidence_claim: REI’s official Marina store page lists a full-service bike shop, trade-in service, used gear, and equipment for hiking, cycling, paddling, and camping.
cards.source_title: REI Marina Store - Marina, CA - Sporting Goods, Camping Gear
cards.access_notes: The official page lists store hours of 10 a.m.–8 p.m. Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–7 p.m. Saturday, and 10 a.m.–6 p.m. Sunday.

cards.title: Consolidate the Supply Run
cards.subtitle: On the General Stilwell Drive retail corridor
cards.notes: Turn onto General Stilwell Drive for one supply stop, and use pickup or Drive Up when hauling dorm, pharmacy, or class essentials.
cards.short_summary: A practical Dunes-area stop offering pickup, pharmacy service, and broad household inventory.
cards.evidence_claim: Target’s official Marina page identifies the General Stilwell Drive store and lists Order Pickup, Drive Up, a CVS pharmacy, and WIC acceptance.
cards.access_notes: Current daily and department hours vary; check the official store page before visiting, particularly for the CVS pharmacy.

cards.title: Choose a Big-Screen Break
cards.subtitle: On the 10th Street entertainment block
cards.notes: Follow 10th Street to the theater, confirm the current rating and showtime on the official schedule, and reserve a seat for a study-break screening.
cards.short_summary: A named cinema block with XD presentation and stadium seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Cinemark’s official theater page locates the cinema at 100 10th Street and lists XD presentation, stadium seating, current films, ratings, and showtimes.
cards.source_title: Movie Theater In Marina, California | Cinemark Century Marina and XD
cards.access_notes: Showtimes and film ratings change daily; consult the official theater page and choose an age-appropriate screening. Admission requires a ticket.

cards.title: Open the Local-History Files
cards.subtitle: On the Harcourt Avenue civic corridor
cards.notes: Stop on Harcourt Avenue and ask library staff about local-history, genealogy, or newspaper microfilm resources before beginning archival research.
cards.short_summary: A civic-corridor library with unusually specific resources for researching Seaside.
cards.evidence_claim: Monterey County says the Seaside Branch provides local-history and genealogy research, local-newspaper microfilm, reference help, and multilingual materials.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday 10 a.m.–6 p.m., Tuesday–Thursday 11 a.m.–7 p.m., and Friday–Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m.

cards.title: Find the City’s Community Rooms
cards.subtitle: On the Hilby Avenue community corridor
cards.notes: Follow Hilby Avenue to the center, check the current activities guide, and contact staff before planning a club meeting or organized group session.
cards.short_summary: A municipal center with rooms ranging from a dance studio to community meeting halls.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Seaside lists six named meeting spaces at the Oldemeyer Center, including a dance studio and Laguna Grande Hall.
cards.access_notes: The city staff directory lists front-office hours as Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–5 p.m.; room use requires arrangements and may involve rental fees.
